todo: The prior depressive-disorder suggestion was withdrawn because the cited systematic review/meta-analysis estimates depression prevalence in multiple sclerosis and reports substantial unexplained heterogeneity but does not establish an MS-to-depression causal or aggravation pathway. Reconsider only with stronger directional evidence and individual development addressing MS phenotype, disability, fatigue, pain, sleep, cognition, treatment, psychosocial factors, and independent psychiatric causes.

suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-12 adds this draft-primary relationship only as a bounded clinical proposition. The review describes optic neuritis as a frequent ocular manifestation of multiple sclerosis and summarizes inflammatory, demyelinating, axonal-degeneration, and remyelination mechanisms linking the two conditions. Require established multiple sclerosis and a separately diagnosed optic-neuritis phenotype compatible with inflammatory demyelinating optic neuropathy. Do not infer optic neuritis from nonspecific visual loss, eye pain, abnormal imaging, or multiple-sclerosis diagnosis alone. Preserve neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder, MOG-antibody disease, ischemic, infectious, compressive, toxic/nutritional, hereditary, and other optic-neuropathy causes. The cited literature supports only this constrained proposition and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.
evidenceGaps: Independent documentation of multiple-sclerosis and optic-neuritis
